{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792774372217,"sessionID":"ses_e9654aae0ffezkhOYrfbmIjNYA","part":{"partID":"prt_169adbb3f0019cHexm97mRQLE5","sessionID":"ses_e9654aae0ffezkhOYrfbmIjNYA","messageID":"msg_169adb537001Yz4OxJfQZfpt85","type":"tool","id":"chatcmpl-tool-a15591feac680006","tool":"write","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"path":"/private/var/folders/8z/h73xmj297g1995r1d9q6dc2r0000gn/T/vw-eval-zml2bhux/work/unicode_truncate.py","content":""""Display-width-aware string truncation.

``truncate`` returns the longest prefix of a text whose display width does
not exceed a given budget.

Display width per code point:

* East Asian Wide / Fullwidth (``unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in
  ('W', 'F')``) counts ``2``.
* A combining mark (``unicodedata.combining(ch) != 0``) counts ``0`` and must
  stay attached to its base character (it is never orphaned).
* Everything else counts ``1``.

A base character and any combining marks immediately following it form a
single atomic cluster: it is either fully included in the prefix or fully
excluded.  Combining marks cost nothing, so including them with their base
never violates the width budget.
"""

import unicodedata

__all__ = ["truncate"]


def _char_width(ch: str) -> int:
    """Display width of a single code point."""
    if unicodedata.east_asian_width(ch) in ("W", "F"):
        return 2
    if unicodedata.combining(ch) != 0:
        return 0
    return 1


def truncate(text: str, max_width: int) -> str:
    """Return the longest prefix of ``text`` with display width <= ``max_width``.

    Args:
        text: The string to truncate.
        max_width: Maximum allowed display width of the returned prefix.

    Returns:
        The longest prefix of ``text`` whose display width is at most
        ``max_width``.  Combining marks are never orphaned from their base
        character: a base and the marks that follow it are kept together.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``text`` is not a ``str``, if ``max_width`` is not an
            ``int`` (``bool`` is rejected), or if ``max_width`` is negative.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise ValueError(
            "text must be a str, got %s" % type(text).__name__
        )
    if isinstance(max_width, bool) or not isinstance(max_width, int):
        raise ValueError(
            "max_width must be an int, got %s" % type(max_width).__name__
        )
    if max_width < 0:
        raise ValueError("max_width must not be negative, got %d" % max_width)

    n = len(text)
    used = 0
    i = 0
    out = []
    while i < n:
        ch = text[i]
        # Cost of the cluster is the width of its first (base) character;
        # any combining marks carried along cost 0.  A run of leading
        # combining marks without a base costs 0 as well and is kept atomic.
        cost = _char_width(ch)
        end = i + 1
        while end < n and unicodedata.combining(text[end]) != 0:
            end += 1
        if used + cost > max_width:
            break
        out.append(text[i:end])
        used += cost
        i = end

    return "".join(out)
